questions.question: Which object does a reverse-mode pullback map to input sensitivity?
questions.explanation: A VJP multiplies an output sensitivity by the transposed Jacobian. A JVP instead propagates an input direction forward.
optionFeedback: A VJP multiplies an output sensitivity by the transposed Jacobian. A JVP instead propagates an input direction forward.
An input direction belongs to a JVP. A VJP takes an output cotangent and maps it back into the input space.
A learning rate belongs to the optimizer. The VJP is a derivative operation and exists before any update rule is chosen.
